name: Murky Green
lede: Murky Green is a dark yellow-green named by an online color survey, using a word that means muddy or dim, and the kind of color a swamp suggests.

sections.title: A mood word
sections.body:
The library records Murky Green only from a 2010 crowd-sourced survey, and the nearest ISCC-NBS category is deep yellow green, about 8.2 units away [1]. Its nearest named relatives are [[olive]], [[olive-green]] and [[moss-green]] [2].

Older color vocabulary has a close cousin. Paterson's *Dictionary of Colour* defines swamp green as a dark murky green, the one place in the books we hold where the phrase appears [3]. It describes a dull water-and-weed color, and no color book treats murky green as a pigment or a dye [3][4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Murky Green appears in 46 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.19%, as photographed [5]. It peaks in paintings of the 1800s, in 12 of 8,345 (0.1%), 1.3 times the rate expected from the same museums [5]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 55% of the 22 paintings where it counts [5]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [5].
